mainTopic: הקב״ה's precision and איוב's words and friends, איוב's daughters, the meaning of אברהם's blessing 'בכל', עשו's sins and ישמעאל's תשובה
overview: This amud finishes the גמרא's reading of הקב״ה's answer to איוב: He times the eagle that catches the mountain goat's kid and the snake that helps the hind give birth to the exact moment, so He would never confuse איוב with אויב. רבא settles two פסוקים that seem to disagree about איוב's words: a person is not held responsible for what he says in pain. The גמרא then describes איוב's three friends, who lived far apart yet came in through one gate together, and רבא praises friendship like theirs. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue whether the birth of daughters brought growth or fighting into the world, and איוב's daughters were doubled in beauty, as their names show. A story about רבי, his son and בר קפרא leads to a dispute among תנאים over what 'בכל' means in אברהם's blessing. Among the answers, עשו did not rebel and ישמעאל did תשובה in אברהם's lifetime. Along the way the גמרא explains why mourners eat lentils, lists עשו's five sins on the day אברהם died, and proves ישמעאל's תשובה from the order of names at אברהם's burial. The amud ends by opening a ברייתא about three people who were given a taste of עולם הבא in this world.

steps.title: The mountain goat and the eagle: perfect timing
steps.stepSummary: הקב״ה describes how He sends an eagle to catch the newborn kid of the mountain goat at exactly the right moment. If He never mixes up one moment with another, He would never mix up איוב with אויב.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the mountain goat gives birth, she climbs to the top of a mountain so the baby falls and dies. But I send an eagle that catches it on its wings and puts it down in front of her. If the eagle came one moment too early or one moment too late, the baby would die at once. I do not mix up one moment with another. Would I mix up איוב with אויב?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues הקב״ה's reply to איוב's complaint. It uses the birth of the mountain goat to show that הקב״ה controls every detail down to the exact moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איוב had complained that הקב״ה confused him with an enemy, since the two words sound almost the same. The answer is an argument from the greater to the lesser: if הקב״ה gets the timing of the eagle exactly right, down to a single moment, He certainly does not confuse two people.

keyTerms.meaning: The mountain goat. The פסוק 'היודע עת לדת יעלי סלע' is about her, and the sentence began just before this section.
Enemy. It sounds almost the same as איוב.

steps.title: The hind and the snake: another example of perfect timing
steps.stepSummary: A second example: the hind has a narrow womb, and הקב״ה sends a snake to bite her at exactly the right moment so she can give birth. Again: no confusing moments, so no confusing איוב with אויב.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Can you watch over the birth pains of the hinds?' The hind has a narrow womb. When she crouches to give birth, I send her a snake that bites her at the opening of the womb, and it loosens so she can give birth. If the snake came one moment early or one moment late, she would die at once. I do not mix up one moment with another. Would I mix up איוב with אויב?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second פסוק from הקב״ה's speech, about the hind (איילה), and reads it the same way as the mountain goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point and the closing line are the same as in step 1, but the case is new. This time the mother herself would die if the timing were off. Repeating the refrain drives home that הקב״ה's precision covers every creature.

phrases.english: "Can you watch over the birth pains of the hinds?" –
phrases.notes: איוב 39:1

phrases.english: this hind, her womb is narrow;
when she crouches to give birth,

and if it came one moment early

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ מְאַחֵר רֶגַע אֶחָד מִיָּד מֵתָה.
phrases.english: or one moment late, she would die immediately.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין רֶגַע לְרֶגַע לֹא נִתְחַלֵּף לִי,
phrases.english: Between one moment and another I do not get confused,
so between Iyov and oyev would I get confused?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel example with the same closing line as step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הקב״ה times the snake's bite to the exact moment, so He would never confuse איוב with אויב.
steps.whatToRemember: Both animal examples make one point: הקב״ה controls every moment exactly, so איוב's complaint that he was mistaken for an enemy cannot be right.

steps.title: Two פסוקים disagree about איוב's words
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק says איוב spoke without knowledge. Another has הקב״ה telling the friends that, unlike His servant איוב, they did not speak correctly. Which is it?
steps.simpleTranslation: It says: 'איוב speaks without knowledge, and his words are without wisdom.' But it is also written: 'For you have not spoken of Me what is right, like My servant איוב'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets two פסוקים against each other. One criticizes איוב's words and the other praises them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If איוב really spoke foolishly, how can הקב״ה praise him for speaking correctly compared to his friends? The contradiction sets up רבא's answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is written. Often used to bring a second פסוק that seems to contradict the first.

phrases.english: "Iyov speaks without knowledge,
phrases.notes: איוב 34:35. The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording, filled in from the פסוק itself.

phrases.english: and his words are without wisdom";
and it is written:
"For you have not spoken of Me what is right
like My servant Iyov"!
phrases.notes: איוב 42:8. הקב״ה says this to the friends.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from הקב״ה's reply to a new question about how איוב's words are judged.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the פסוקים judge איוב's speech
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק condemns איוב's words as foolish, while another praises them over his friends' words. Both cannot be fully true as they stand.

steps.title: רבא: a person in pain is not held responsible for his words
steps.stepSummary: רבא resolves the contradiction: איוב's words were wrong, but he is not held responsible for them because he spoke in pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From here we learn that a person is not held responsible for what he says when he is in pain.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the contradiction from step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים are true. איוב's words really were without wisdom, but since he said them while suffering, they are not held against him, and הקב״ה can still call him 'My servant' who spoke rightly. This becomes a general principle about anyone in pain.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time of his pain or suffering

steps.whatToRemember: A person is not held responsible for what he says in a time of pain (רבא).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a lasting principle about judging people kindly. Harsh words said in suffering are not counted against the speaker the way they normally would be.

phrases.english: Rava said:
From here we learn that a person is not held responsible
at the time of his pain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reconciles the two פסוקים: both are true, from different angles.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either איוב's words were foolish and he deserves blame, or they were right and the criticism is wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: His words were improper, but he is not held responsible because he spoke in pain.

steps.title: What does 'ויועדו יחדו' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about איוב's three friends coming to comfort him and asks what the phrase 'they met together' teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And איוב's three friends heard about all this evil that had come upon him, and each came from his own place: אליפז the Temanite, בלדד the Shuhite, and צופר the Naamathite. And they met together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him.' What does 'they met together' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the arrival of איוב's friends. It asks about one phrase in the פסוק, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already says each came 'from his own place,' so 'they met together' seems to add something. The גמרא wants to know what extra detail this phrase teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: And they met (or set a meeting) together
To show him sympathy, to mourn with him

phrases.english: "And Iyov's three friends heard
phrases.notes: איוב 2:11

phrases.aramaic: אֵת כׇּל הָרָעָה הַזֹּאת הַבָּאָה עָלָיו,
phrases.english: of all this evil that had come upon him,
and they came, each man from his own place –
Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite
and Zophar the Naamathite,
and they met together
to come to mourn with him and to comfort him" –
What does "they met together" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about איוב's friends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the phrase 'ויועדו יחדו' adds to the פסוק.

steps.title: רב: they all entered through one gate
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, explains that 'they met together' means all three friends came in through one gate at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This teaches that they all came in through one gate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Together' is read literally: the three friends did not arrive one after another. They came in at the same moment, through the same gate.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
This teaches that they all entered through one gate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מְלַמֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three friends all entered through one gate at the same time.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the friends lived three hundred פרסאות apart
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that each friend lived three hundred פרסאות away from the others, which makes their arriving together even more striking.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: Between each one of them there were three hundred פרסאות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a ברייתא with a new detail about how far apart the friends lived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said they entered through one gate together. The ברייתא adds that they lived very far from each other, so arriving at the same moment was remarkable.

keyTerms.meaning: פרסאות, a measure of distance (about four מילין each)

phrases.english: And it was taught:
Between each and every one of them
there were three hundred parasangs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail that makes רב's teaching in step 6 more striking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of איוב's three friends lived three hundred פרסאות from the others.

steps.title: How did the friends know?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how all three friends found out about איוב's troubles at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did they know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. If the friends lived so far apart and still arrived together, how did they all learn about איוב's suffering at the same moment? This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said each friend lived three hundred פרסאות away from the others. With that distance, arriving through one gate together needs an explanation. The question is about how the news reached them.

phrases.english: How did they know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the striking event in steps 6–7 was possible.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the three distant friends learned of איוב's suffering at the same moment.

steps.title: A crown or trees gave them the sign
steps.stepSummary: Two opinions: each friend had a special crown, or special trees that withered when trouble came to one of the others.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say they each had a crown. Others say they each had trees, and when the trees withered they knew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two answers. Either each friend had a crown that showed a sign, or each had trees that dried up when one of the group was in trouble.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both answers say the friends had a warning sign that worked at a distance. That explains how all three learned the news at once, and so how they could arrive together.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (introduces an opinion)

phrases.english: There are those who say: they had a crown.
phrases.notes: Each friend had a crown that showed a sign when something happened to one of the others.

phrases.english: And there are those who say: they had trees,
and once they withered, they knew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They had a sign, either a crown or trees that withered, that told them when one of the group was in trouble.

steps.title: A friend like איוב's friends, or death
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the loyalty of איוב's friends explains the popular saying: either a friend like איוב's friends, or death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is what people mean when they say: Either a friend like the friends of איוב, or death.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא connects the story to a common saying. Friends this close are so valuable that life without them is hardly worth living.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The friends were so bound together that they had signs telling them when one was suffering, and they came right away. רבא uses this to explain the saying: a person needs friends like that, and without them it is as if he is dead.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (a popular saying)

steps.whatToRemember: איוב's friends were deeply loyal. They knew of his pain from far away and came together to comfort him. רבא uses this as the model of true friendship.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is what people say:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ חַבְרָא כְּחַבְרֵי דְּאִיּוֹב, אוֹ מִיתוּתָא.
phrases.english: Either a friend like the friends of Job, or death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a lesson from the friends' closeness described in steps 6–9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Close, loyal friendship like that of איוב's friends is essential. Without it, life is like death.

steps.title: What came into the world when daughters were born
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק about daughters being born, רבי יוחנן says having children increased in the world, and ריש לקיש says fighting came into the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And it came to pass, when man began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born to them.' רבי יוחנן says: Having children came into the world. ריש לקיש says: Fighting came into the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a פסוק from בראשית. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש disagree about what the birth of daughters brought into the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לָרֹב can be read as רְבִיָּיה, having many children, or as מְרִיבָה, fighting. רבי יוחנן sees daughters as a blessing that grows the world. ריש לקיש sees them as a cause of fighting between men. This disagreement sets up the challenge about איוב in the next step.

phrases.english: "And it came to pass, when man began to multiply
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:1

phrases.aramaic: עַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, וּבָנוֹת יֻלְּדוּ לָהֶם״ –
phrases.english: on the face of the earth, and daughters were born to them" –

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: רְבִיָּיה בָּאָה לְעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: propagation came to the world.

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מְרִיבָה בָּאָה לָעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: Reish Lakish says: strife came to the world.
phrases.notes: He reads לָרֹב as if it were connected to מְרִיבָה. Once there were daughters, men fought over them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיְהִי כִּי הֵחֵל הָאָדָם לָרֹב עַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic that will lead back to איוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: daughters brought growth in numbers to the world. ריש לקיש: daughters brought fighting to the world.

steps.title: Why weren't איוב's daughters doubled?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן: if daughters are a blessing, why were איוב's daughters not doubled when everything else he had was doubled?
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to רבי יוחנן: According to you, who say daughters brought growth to the world, why weren't איוב's daughters doubled?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש attacks רבי יוחנן's view using איוב. At the end of the story everything איוב had was doubled, but he still had only three daughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If daughters are a blessing, as רבי יוחנן says, then איוב should have gotten six daughters instead of three when הקב״ה doubled his blessings. Since the number stayed at three, it seems daughters are not counted as a blessing. That would fit ריש לקיש's view.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to Rabbi Yoḥanan:
According to you, who say propagation came to the world,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נִכְפְּלוּ בְּנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אִיּוֹב?
phrases.english: for what reason were Job's daughters not doubled?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לְדִידָךְ דְּאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's opinion from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that daughters are a blessing of growth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If daughters were a blessing, איוב's daughters would have been doubled along with everything else. They were not.

steps.title: Doubled in beauty, not in number
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the daughters were not doubled in number, but they were doubled in beauty, as their names show.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: True, they were not doubled in number, but they were doubled in beauty. As it is written: 'He had seven sons and three daughters. He called the first one ימימה, the second קציעה, and the third קרן הפוך.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש. The blessing of the daughters was doubled in a different way: in how beautiful they were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן admits the number stayed the same. He says the doubling came in quality instead of quantity. His proof is the פסוק that gives the daughters' names, which the גמרא will explain next as names of beauty.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: נְהִי דְּלֹא נִכְפְּלוּ בְּשֵׁמוֹת,
phrases.english: He said to him: Granted that they were not doubled in name,
phrases.notes: "In name" means in how many separate daughters there were.

phrases.english: but they were doubled in beauty, as it is written:
"He had seven sons and three daughters.
And he called the name of the first Jemimah,
and the name of the second Keziah,
and the name of the third Keren-happuch."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: נְהִי דְּלֹא נִכְפְּלוּ בְּשֵׁמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's challenge from step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the doubling: in quality instead of quantity.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the number of daughters was not doubled, daughters must not count as a blessing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The daughters were doubled in beauty, which the פסוק hints at through their names.

steps.title: The meaning of the first two names
steps.stepSummary: ימימה means she was bright like the day. קציעה means she smelled like the cassia spice.
steps.simpleTranslation: ימימה: she was like the day. קציעה: her scent spread like cassia.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first two daughters' names to show that each one describes beauty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ימימה comes from יוֹם, day, meaning she was bright and radiant. קציעה is a sweet-smelling spice, meaning her scent was lovely. These explanations back up רבי יוחנן's claim that the names describe extra beauty.

phrases.english: Jemimah: she was similar to the day.
Keziah: her scent spread like cassia.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the names quoted in step 13 to support the claim about beauty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names ימימה and קציעה describe radiance and fragrance.

steps.title: Third name: like the horn of a קרש
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי שילא explain קרן הפוך as meaning she looked like the horn of a קרש, an animal with beautiful horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: קרן הפוך: in the school of רבי שילא they say she was like the horn of a קרש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first explanation of the third name. It reads קֶרֶן as the horn of a קרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explanation takes the word קֶרֶן, horn, literally and compares the daughter to a beautiful animal horn. The next step will challenge this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The horn of a קרש, a kind of animal

phrases.aramaic: קֶרֶן הַפּוּךְ – אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי שֵׁילָא:
phrases.english: Keren-happuch: they say in the school of Rabbi Sheila:
that she was similar to the horn of a keresh.

steps.triggerLanguage: קֶרֶן הַפּוּךְ – אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי שֵׁילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the names, now the third one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קרן הפוך means she looked like the horn of a קרש.

steps.title: In the West they laughed at that
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they laughed at this explanation, since looking like a קרש's horn is a defect, not beauty.
steps.simpleTranslation: They laughed at this in the West: the horn of a קרש is a defect!
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars of ארץ ישראל reject the previous explanation. Comparing a girl to an animal horn sounds like a flaw, not a compliment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole point of the names is to show extra beauty. An explanation that makes the third daughter sound blemished defeats that purpose, so it is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: "The West" (מַעְרְבָא) is not some faraway western country. It means ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל, where the גמרא was written.

phrases.english: They laughed at this in the West,
the horn of a keresh is a defect!
phrases.notes: For a person to look like that horn would be a blemish, not beauty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the explanation given in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the explanation of קרן הפוך as the horn of a קרש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Looking like a קרש's horn is a blemish, which goes against the point that the names describe beauty.

steps.title: רב חסדא: like the finest garden saffron
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains קרן הפוך as meaning she was like garden saffron, the best of its kind, and brings a פסוק showing that פוך means beauty makeup.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חסדא said: She was like garden saffron, the best of its kind, as it says: 'Though you paint your eyes with פוך.'
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the horn explanation, the גמרא brings רב חסדא's explanation instead. It does show beauty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא reads קֶרֶן as connected to a garden and פּוּךְ as eye makeup used to look beautiful. He proves the meaning of פוך from a פסוק in ירמיהו. So the third name also describes outstanding beauty, and רבי יוחנן's answer holds.
steps.whatToRemember: All three of איוב's daughters' names describe beauty. This supports רבי יוחנן: the daughters were doubled in beauty, so daughters are still a blessing.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ḥisda said:
like garden saffron, the best of its kind –
as it is stated: "Though you enlarge your eyes with paint."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 4:30

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation rejected in step 16 with a new one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קרן הפוך means she was like the finest garden saffron. פוך means beauty makeup, as the פסוק in ירמיהו shows.

steps.title: רבי comforts his son over the birth of a daughter
steps.stepSummary: A daughter is born to רבי שמעון, son of רבי, and he is upset. His father comforts him by saying that more people have come into the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: A daughter was born to רבי שמעון the son of רבי, and he was upset. His father said to him: Increase has come to the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. רבי שמעון is upset that he had a daughter, and his father רבי tries to comfort him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's comfort is that any child, boy or girl, adds to the world's population. This is a positive view of having a daughter, and the next step will push back against it.

keyTerms.meaning: He was upset, literally 'his mind became weak'

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי אִיתְיְלִידָא לֵיהּ בְּרַתָּא,
phrases.english: A daughter was born to רבי שמעון, son of רבי,
phrases.notes: 'רבי' here means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה.

phrases.english: and he was upset.
His father said to him:
Increase has come to the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי אִיתְיְלִידָא לֵיהּ בְּרַתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of blessings in children (איוב's daughters) with a new story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Having a daughter adds to the world's population, so it is a reason to be comforted.

steps.title: בר קפרא calls the comfort empty
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא tells רבי שמעון that his father's comfort means nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא said to him: Your father comforted you with empty comfort.
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא rejects רבי's words of comfort and calls them empty. His proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר קפרא does not deny that daughters add to the world. He argues that this fact alone does not make having a daughter a personal blessing for the father.

keyTerms.meaning: Emptiness, something with no real value

phrases.english: בר קפרא said to him:
Your father has comforted you with empty comfort,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי's comfort from Step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי's claim that the world's increase is a reason to be comforted over having a daughter.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Something needed by the world in general is not necessarily good for the individual who has it.

steps.title: The ברייתא: the world needs both, but some roles are better
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא brings a ברייתא: the world needs both males and females, just as it needs both spice sellers and tanners, but it is better to have the more pleasant one.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: The world cannot exist without males and without females. But fortunate is the one whose children are males, and woe to the one whose children are females. The world cannot exist without a spice seller and without a tanner. Fortunate is the one whose job is spice selling, and woe to the one whose job is tanning.
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא backs up his rejection with a ברייתא. It uses the example of spice sellers and tanners to show that something the world needs can still be unpleasant for the person who does it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא agrees that the world needs both. Its point is that 'the world needs it' does not mean 'it is good for you'. That is exactly why רבי's comfort was empty in בר קפרא's eyes.

keyTerms.meaning: A spice seller, whose work smells good
A tanner, whose work with hides smells bad

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have these words; the square brackets show they belong in the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָעוֹלָם בְּלֹא זְכָרִים וּבְלֹא נְקֵבוֹת;
phrases.english: The world cannot exist without males and without females;
but fortunate is the one whose children are males,
and woe to the one whose children are females.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָעוֹלָם בְּלֹא בַּסָּם וּבְלֹא בּוּרְסִי;
phrases.english: The world cannot exist without a spice seller and without a tanner;
fortunate is the one whose job is spice selling,
woe to the one whose job is tanning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind בר קפרא's rejection in Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: בר קפרא's claim that רבי's comfort was empty.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא comparing males and females to spice sellers and tanners.

steps.title: A dispute among תנאים: was אברהם blessed with no daughter or with a daughter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this is like a dispute among תנאים about the word 'בכל' in אברהם's blessing. רבי מאיר says the blessing was having no daughter, and רבי יהודה says the blessing was having a daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute among תנאים: 'And ה׳ blessed אברהם with everything.' What is 'with everything'? רבי מאיר says: That he did not have a daughter. רבי יהודה says: That he did have a daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the question of whether a daughter is a blessing was already argued by תנאים. They argued about what 'בכל' means in אברהם's blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's view matches בר קפרא, since having no daughter was the blessing. רבי יהודה's view matches רבי, since a daughter is itself a blessing. So the two positions in the story line up with an older dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: This is like a dispute among תנאים

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the story about רבי and בר קפרא reflects an older debate, and that both views have strong backing.

phrases.english: This is like a dispute among תנאים:
'And ה׳ blessed Avraham with everything' —
phrases.notes: בראשית 24:1

phrases.english: What is 'with everything'?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה לוֹ בַּת.
phrases.english: רבי מאיר says: That he did not have a daughter.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שֶׁהָיְתָה לוֹ בַּת.
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: That he had a daughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the רבי and בר קפרא debate to a dispute among תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: אברהם's blessing was having no daughter. רבי יהודה: his blessing was having a daughter.

steps.title: Others: אברהם's daughter was named בכל
steps.stepSummary: A third opinion says אברהם had a daughter whose name was בכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say: אברהם had a daughter, and her name was 'בכל'.
steps.whatsHappening: Another opinion reads 'בכל' as the actual name of אברהם's daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opinion agrees with רבי יהודה that אברהם had a daughter. It adds that the word in the פסוק is her name, so the פסוק means that אברהם was blessed with her.

phrases.english: Others say:

phrases.aramaic: בַּת הָיְתָה לוֹ לְאַבְרָהָם, וּ״בַכֹּל״ שְׁמָהּ.
phrases.english: Avraham had a daughter, and 'בכל' was her name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third reading of 'בכל'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'בכל' was the name of אברהם's daughter.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר המודעי: אברהם's wisdom in the stars
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר המודעי says the blessing was אברהם's great knowledge of the stars, which brought all the kings to his door.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר המודעי says: אברהם our father had knowledge of the stars in his heart, so that all the kings of the east and west would come early to his door.
steps.whatsHappening: Another opinion explains 'בכל' differently. אברהם had knowledge of the stars that everyone needed, so kings came to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the blessing has nothing to do with children. 'Everything' means that אברהם had something that everyone, even kings, came to get from him.

keyTerms.meaning: Knowledge of the stars and how they affect events
Came early to his door, meaning they came eagerly to seek his help

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר המודעי says:

phrases.aramaic: אִיצְטַגְנִינוּת הָיְתָה בְּלִבּוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ,
phrases.english: Knowledge of the stars was in the heart of Avraham our father,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכׇּל מַלְכֵי מִזְרָח וּמַעֲרָב מַשְׁכִּימִין לְפִתְחוֹ.
phrases.english: so that all the kings of the east and west would come early to his door.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another reading of 'בכל'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'בכל' means אברהם's knowledge of the stars, which everyone came to seek.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחי: אברהם's healing stone
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says אברהם wore a precious stone that healed the sick. When he died, ה׳ hung it on the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: A precious stone hung on the neck of אברהם our father, and any sick person who saw it was healed right away. When אברהם our father left the world, the Holy One, Blessed be He, hung it on the sphere of the sun.
steps.whatsHappening: Another opinion says 'בכל' refers to a healing stone that אברהם wore around his neck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the previous opinion, the blessing here is something that benefited everyone. After אברהם's death the healing power did not disappear; it moved to the sun.

phrases.english: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says:

phrases.aramaic: אֶבֶן טוֹבָה הָיְתָה תְּלוּיָה בְּצַוָּארוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ,
phrases.english: A precious stone hung on the neck of Avraham our father,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכׇּל חוֹלֶה הָרוֹאֶה אוֹתוֹ מִיָּד מִתְרַפֵּא;
phrases.english: so that any sick person who saw it was healed right away;

phrases.aramaic: וּבְשָׁעָה שֶׁנִּפְטַר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ מִן הָעוֹלָם –
phrases.english: and when Avraham our father left the world,

phrases.aramaic: תְּלָאָהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּגַלְגַּל חַמָּה.
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, hung it on the sphere of the sun.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another reading of 'בכל'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'בכל' means a healing stone that אברהם wore, which was later placed in the sun.

steps.title: אביי: the popular saying about sickness and daylight
steps.stepSummary: אביי connects רבי שמעון בן יוחי's teaching to a popular saying: as the day rises, sickness lifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what people say: As the day rises, the sickness lifts.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי shows that a common saying fits רבי שמעון בן יוחי's teaching about the healing stone in the sun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the healing stone hangs on the sun, then sick people should feel better as the sun climbs higher. אביי says this explains the folk saying.

phrases.english: אביי said: This is what people say:
As the day rises, the sickness lifts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 24 with a popular saying.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון בן יוחי's claim that the healing stone hangs on the sun.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The folk saying 'As the day rises, the sickness lifts'.

steps.title: Two more explanations: עשו did not rebel, and ישמעאל did תשובה
steps.stepSummary: Two more readings of 'בכל': עשו did not rebel during אברהם's lifetime, and ישמעאל did תשובה during his lifetime.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: That עשו did not rebel in his days. Another explanation: That ישמעאל did תשובה in his days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two more meanings of 'בכל'. Both are about אברהם's family behaving well while he was alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the blessing is about אברהם's descendants in his lifetime: he did not see עשו's wickedness, and he saw ישמעאל do תשובה. The next steps prove the first claim, about עשו.

keyTerms.meaning: Rebelled, meaning he turned to sin

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר אַחֵר: שֶׁלֹּא מָרַד עֵשָׂו בְּיָמָיו.
phrases.english: Another explanation: That עשו did not rebel in his days.

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר אַחֵר: שֶׁעָשָׂה יִשְׁמָעֵאל תְּשׁוּבָה בְּיָמָיו.
phrases.english: Another explanation: That ישמעאל did תשובה in his days.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: שֶׁלֹּא מָרַד עֵשָׂו בְּיָמָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds two more readings of 'בכל'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'בכל' means that during אברהם's lifetime עשו did not sin and ישמעאל did תשובה.

steps.title: How do we know עשו did not rebel in אברהם's lifetime?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that עשו did not rebel while אברהם was alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: That עשו did not rebel in his days, from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof of the claim about עשו. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim about עשו is not stated openly in the פסוקים, so the גמרא wants to see where it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: That עשו did not rebel in his days, from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first claim in Step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that עשו did not sin while אברהם was alive.

steps.title: The day עשו came in tired was the day אברהם died
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says עשו came in from the field tired, and a ברייתא teaches that this was the day אברהם died, when יעקב cooked lentils to comfort יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And עשו came in from the field, and he was tired.' And it was taught: On that day אברהם our father died, and יעקב our father cooked a lentil stew to comfort יצחק his father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק and a ברייתא. The day עשו came in 'tired' was the same day אברהם died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב was cooking lentils because the family was in mourning for אברהם. So the day עשו came in tired, the day his bad behavior began, came only after אברהם's death. This shows he had not rebelled while אברהם was alive.

phrases.english: As it is written:
'And עשו came in from the field, and he was tired,'
phrases.notes: בראשית 25:29

phrases.aramaic: וְתָנָא: אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם נִפְטַר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ,
phrases.english: and it was taught: On that day Avraham our father died,

phrases.aramaic: וְעָשָׂה יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ תַּבְשִׁיל שֶׁל עֲדָשִׁים
phrases.english: and Yaakov our father made a lentil stew
to comfort Yitzchak his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The day עשו came in tired was the day אברהם died, so his rebellion began only after אברהם's death.

steps.title: Why lentils for a mourner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why lentils in particular were served to comfort a mourner.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is special about lentils?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא mentioned lentils for mourners, so the גמרא asks why lentils were chosen. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side question that comes from the detail of the lentil stew in Step 28. It turns the discussion toward the customs of mourning.

phrases.english: And what is different about lentils?
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have this question; the square brackets show it belongs in the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a detail from Step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason lentils are the food for mourners.

steps.title: A lentil has no mouth, and neither does a mourner
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they said in the name of רבה בר מרי: a lentil has no opening, just as a mourner has no 'mouth'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say in the West in the name of רבה בר מרי: Just as this lentil has no mouth, so too a mourner has no mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: a lentil has no opening, and that matches a mourner, who is too pained to speak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other beans have a slit that looks like a mouth, but a lentil does not. The lentil is a symbol of the mourner's silence.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר מָרִי:
phrases.english: They say in the West in the name of רבה בר מרי:
phrases.notes: 'The West' is ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל.

phrases.aramaic: מָה עֲדָשָׁה זוֹ אֵין לָהּ פֶּה,
phrases.english: Just as this lentil has no mouth,
phrases.notes: Many beans have a little slit that looks like a mouth; a lentil does not.

phrases.english: so too a mourner has no mouth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר מָרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lentils have no opening, which matches the silence of a mourner.

steps.title: A lentil is round, and mourning comes around to everyone
steps.stepSummary: A second reason: a lentil is round, just as mourning rolls around and comes to every person in the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: Just as this lentil is round, so too mourning rolls around and comes back to everyone in the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second reason for lentils. Their round shape stands for mourning, which goes around to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason focuses on the round shape, not on the missing opening. The message is that every person will face mourning at some point.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone in the world, literally 'those who come into the world'

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר אַחֵר: מָה עֲדָשָׁה זוֹ מְגוּלְגֶּלֶת,
phrases.english: Another explanation: Just as this lentil is round,
so too mourning rolls around
and comes back to everyone in the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: מָה עֲדָשָׁה זוֹ מְגוּלְגֶּלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of Step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lentils are served because their round shape stands for mourning coming around to everyone.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two reasons for lentils.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two reasons ever lead to a different result. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons explain lentils equally well, so the גמרא looks for a case where they would disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the reasons from Steps 30 and 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where the two reasons would lead to different results.

steps.title: The difference: comforting a mourner with eggs
steps.stepSummary: The difference is whether eggs may be served to comfort a mourner.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: whether to comfort a mourner with eggs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two reasons differ about eggs. Eggs have no opening, but they are not perfectly round.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the 'no mouth' reason, eggs are fitting for a mourner. By the 'round' reason they are not, since an egg is not fully round.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: Two reasons are given for serving lentils to mourners: they have no 'mouth', like a silent mourner, and they are round, like mourning that comes around to everyone. The practical difference between the reasons is whether eggs may be served.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: comforting with eggs.
phrases.notes: An egg has no opening, but it isn't perfectly round, so the two reasons give different answers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Eggs fit the 'no mouth' reason but not the 'round' reason.

steps.title: עשו's five sins on that day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says עשו committed five sins on the day אברהם died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: That wicked man (עשו) committed five sins on that day. He was with a betrothed young woman, he killed a person, he denied belief in God, he denied תחיית המתים, and he scorned the birthright.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a list of five terrible sins that עשו did on the day אברהם died. The next steps will bring a source for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new statement that opens a short list. Each item will be tied to a word in the story of עשו selling the בכורה (בראשית 25). The claim is that all five happened on one day.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed young woman (after אירוסין, before full marriage)
Denied the main principle, meaning belief in God

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
That wicked one committed five sins
phrases.notes: 'That wicked one' is עשו, and 'that day' is the day אברהם died, which the גמרא was just discussing.

phrases.english: on that day:
he had relations with a betrothed young woman,
and he killed a person,
and he denied the fundamental principle,
phrases.notes: The 'fundamental principle' means belief in God Himself.

phrases.english: and he denied the resurrection of the dead,
and he scorned the birthright.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: חָמֵשׁ עֲבֵירוֹת עָבַר אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע בְּאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the lentils served to a mourner (steps 29-33) to what עשו did on the day אברהם died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עשו committed five sins on the day אברהם died.

steps.title: Source for the sin with a betrothed young woman
steps.stepSummary: The word 'field' links עשו coming from the field to the betrothed young woman attacked in a field.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was with a betrothed young woman: here it says 'and עשו came in from the field,' and there it says 'for he found her in the field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the first sin by matching the word 'שדה' (field) in two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים about a field is talking about a betrothed young woman who was attacked. Because the same word appears in עשו's story, the גמרא reads his 'coming from the field' as hinting at that same sin.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here (in our story)
And it is written there (in another place)
Field, the word that links the two פסוקים

phrases.english: He had relations with a betrothed young woman:
it is written here: 'And Esau came in from the field,'
phrases.notes: בראשית 25:29

phrases.english: and it is written there: 'For he found her in the field.'
phrases.notes: דברים 22:27, which is about a betrothed young woman attacked in a field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the first sin listed in step 34.
steps.raayaObject: That עשו sinned with a betrothed young woman.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared word 'שדה' in בראשית 25:29 and דברים 22:27.

steps.title: Source for killing a person
steps.stepSummary: The word 'tired' (עיף) links עשו to the tiredness that comes from killers.
steps.simpleTranslation: He killed a person: here it says 'tired,' and there it says 'Woe is me, for my soul is tired because of the killers.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the second sin by matching the word 'עיף' (tired).
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ירמיהו, being 'tired' is connected to killers. So when the תורה says עשו came home tired, the גמרא reads it as a hint that he had killed someone.

keyTerms.meaning: Tired or faint, the linking word

phrases.english: He killed a person:
it is written here: 'tired,'
phrases.notes: From the same פסוק, בראשית 25:29: עשו came from the field, and he was tired.

phrases.english: and it is written there:

phrases.aramaic: ״אוֹי נָא לִי כִּי עָיְפָה נַפְשִׁי לְהֹרְגִים״.
phrases.english: 'Woe is me, for my soul is faint because of the killers.'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 4:31

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the second sin in the list.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared word 'עיף' in בראשית 25:29 and ירמיהו 4:31.

steps.title: Source for denying God
steps.stepSummary: The word 'this' (זה) links עשו's words to 'this is my God.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He denied the fundamental principle: here it says 'why is this to me,' and there it says 'this is my God and I will glorify Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the third sin by matching the word 'זה' (this).
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the sea, the Jews said 'זה אלי,' meaning 'this is my God.' So when עשו asked 'what use is this to me,' the גמרא hears him saying 'what use is God to me,' which is a denial of God.

keyTerms.meaning: Why is this to me? (what good is it to me)
This is my God and I will glorify Him

phrases.english: And he denied the fundamental principle:
it is written here: 'What use is this to me,'
phrases.notes: בראשית 25:32

phrases.english: and it is written there: 'This is my God and I will glorify Him.'
phrases.notes: שמות 15:2. The shared word is 'זה,' so 'this' in עשו's mouth is read as 'my God.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the third sin in the list.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared word 'זה' in בראשית 25:32 and שמות 15:2.

steps.title: Sources for denying resurrection and scorning the birthright
steps.stepSummary: The last two sins are proven directly from עשו's own words and from the פסוק about the בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He denied תחיית המתים, as it says: 'Behold, I am going to die.' And he scorned the birthright, as it says: 'And עשו scorned the birthright.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list by bringing direct פסוקים for the last two sins, with no word-matching needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עשו's words 'I am going to die' show he thought death is the end, so he did not believe in תחיית המתים. The last sin, scorning the בכורה, is stated openly in the פסוק.
steps.whatToRemember: Each of עשו's five sins is tied to the בכורה story: three through matching words, and two through direct פסוקים.

phrases.english: And he denied the resurrection of the dead:
as it is written: 'Behold, I am going to die.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 25:32

phrases.english: And he scorned the birthright:
as it is written: 'And Esau scorned the birthright.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 25:34

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the sources for the list in step 34.
steps.raayaObject: That עשו denied תחיית המתים and scorned the בכורה.

steps.title: How do we know ישמעאל repented?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that ישמעאל did תשובה while אברהם was alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that ישמעאל did תשובה in his days, how do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to an earlier claim on the daf, that ישמעאל did תשובה in אברהם's lifetime, and asks for its source. This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא had counted ישמעאל's תשובה as one of the blessings אברהם received. Now it wants a proof that this really happened.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it?

phrases.english: And that Ishmael repented in his days,
phrases.notes: 'His days' means while אברהם was still alive, which is a claim made earlier on this daf.

phrases.english: from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the עשו discussion and goes back to an earlier claim about ישמעאל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that ישמעאל did תשובה in אברהם's lifetime.

steps.title: רבינא asks about the word 'גויעה'
steps.stepSummary: While רבא dozes, רבינא asks רב חמא בר בוזי whether every death described with 'גויעה' is the death of a צדיק, and he says yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like the story of רבינא and רב חמא בר בוזי, who were sitting before רבא while רבא was dozing. רבינא said to רב חמא בר בוזי: Is it true that you say every death described with 'גויעה' is the death of צדיקים? He said: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that will answer the question. In it, רבינא checks a rule held by רב חמא בר בוזי, and he confirms it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that the word 'ויגוע' (he expired) is used only for the death of a צדיק. This rule will soon be tested against ישמעאל, which is how the story connects to our question.

keyTerms.meaning: Expiring, from the word 'ויגוע' used for death

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרָבִינָא וְרַב חָמָא בַּר בּוּזִי
phrases.english: As in this case of Ravina and Rav Chama bar Buzi,
who were sitting before Rava,
and Rava was dozing.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב חָמָא בַּר בּוּזִי,
phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Chama bar Buzi:
Is it true that you say:
any death that has 'expiring' written about it,
that is the death of the righteous?
He said to him: Yes.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרָבִינָא וְרַב חָמָא בַּר בּוּזִי הֲווֹ יָתְבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the story that will answer the question in step 39.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'גויעה' always marks the death of a צדיק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, according to רב חמא בר בוזי.

steps.title: The generation of the flood
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges the rule: the generation of the flood is described with 'גויעה', and they were wicked.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the generation of the flood?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks the rule with a counterexample: the wicked people of the flood are also described with 'ויגוע.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'גויעה' only means a צדיק's death, it should never be used for the דור המבול, who died because they were wicked. So the rule as stated seems too broad.

phrases.english: But what about the generation of the flood!
phrases.notes: There the פסוק says 'ויגוע כל בשר,' all flesh expired (בראשית 7:21).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule just confirmed in step 40.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that 'גויעה' always marks a צדיק's death.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The דור המבול were wicked, yet the פסוק uses 'גויעה' about them.

steps.title: Only 'גויעה' together with 'אסיפה'
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בר בוזי narrows the rule: it applies only when both 'גויעה' and 'אסיפה' appear.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We are talking about 'expiring' together with 'being gathered.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא בר בוזי answers by making the rule narrower. Only when both words appear does it mean a צדיק's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The דור המבול has only 'גויעה,' not 'אסיפה' (being gathered to one's people). So the counterexample no longer works against the narrower rule.

phrases.english: He said to him:
We are speaking of 'expiring' together with 'being gathered.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 41.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only 'גויעה' together with 'אסיפה' marks a צדיק's death.

steps.title: But ישמעאל has both words
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges again: ישמעאל's death has both 'גויעה' and 'אסיפה', yet he seems to be a רשע.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about ישמעאל, about whom both 'expiring' and 'being gathered' are written?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes back against the narrower rule. ישמעאל's death uses both words, so was he a צדיק?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the narrower rule seems to fail, because ישמעאל is known as wicked. This challenge sets up the answer that ties back to the question of step 39.

phrases.english: But what about Ishmael,
about whom 'expiring' and 'being gathered' are written!
phrases.notes: בראשית 25:17

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the narrowed rule from step 42.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that 'גויעה' with 'אסיפה' marks a צדיק's death.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ישמעאל has both words, yet he is thought of as wicked.

steps.title: רבא wakes up: ישמעאל repented
steps.stepSummary: רבא wakes and quotes רבי יוחנן: ישמעאל did תשובה in his father's lifetime, as shown by the burial פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile רבא woke up and said to them: Children, this is what רבי יוחנן said: ישמעאל did תשובה in his father's lifetime, as it says: 'And his sons יצחק and ישמעאל buried him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא wakes up and settles the argument. ישמעאל really did die as a צדיק, because he had done תשובה, and that also answers our question from step 39.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the burial פסוק, יצחק is named before ישמעאל even though ישמעאל was older. This shows ישמעאל let יצחק lead, a sign that he had changed his ways. So the rule about 'גויעה' with 'אסיפה' stands, and we now have the source for ישמעאל's תשובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Children, a teasing way of saying 'youngsters'

steps.whatToRemember: ישמעאל did תשובה while אברהם was alive. That is why his death is described with 'גויעה' and 'אסיפה', the way a צדיק's death is described.

phrases.english: In the meantime Rava woke up to them,
he said to them: Children,
this is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
Ishmael repented in his father's lifetime,
as it is said: 'And Isaac and Ishmael, his sons, buried him.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 25:9. יצחק is named first even though ישמעאל was older, which shows ישמעאל let him lead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 43 and answers the question of step 39.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual answer: the case is not a real counterexample
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ישמעאל died a רשע, so the rule must be wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: ישמעאל did תשובה, so he died a צדיק and the rule holds.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the burial פסוק, where ישמעאל lets יצחק go first.

steps.title: Maybe the order is by wisdom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof: maybe the פסוק lists יצחק first only because he was wiser.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the פסוק lists them in the order of their wisdom!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in רבי יוחנן's proof from the burial פסוק. Maybe יצחק comes first just because he was the wiser brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's proof depended on ישמעאל letting יצחק go ahead of him. If the Torah lists people by wisdom anyway, the order tells us nothing about ישמעאל's behavior. Then there is no proof that he did תשובה.

keyTerms.meaning: But maybe (opens a possible other reading)
In the order of their wisdom

phrases.english: But perhaps in the order of their wisdom
phrases.notes: This is about the פסוק from the last step: "וַיִּקְבְּרוּ אֹתוֹ יִצְחָק וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל" (בראשית 25:9).

phrases.english: it lists them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא דֶּרֶךְ חׇכְמָתָן קָא חָשֵׁיב לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof רבא brought in the name of רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the order in the burial פסוק shows ישמעאל gave way to יצחק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The order could come from the brothers' wisdom, so it says nothing about ישמעאל's תשובה.

steps.title: The burial of יצחק shows the Torah does not list by wisdom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge: at יצחק's burial, עשו is listed before the wiser יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, the פסוק says: "And עשו and יעקב, his sons, buried him." Why does it not list them in the order of their wisdom there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with another burial פסוק. There עשו comes before יעקב, even though יעקב was clearly the wiser one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah listed sons by wisdom, יעקב should come before עשו at יצחק's burial. Since it does not, the Torah does not order burial lists by wisdom. So the challenge in step 45 falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (pushes an idea to a result that cannot be right)
עשו and יעקב, the sons of יצחק

phrases.english: But if that is so,
"And Esau and Jacob, his sons, buried him"
phrases.notes: בראשית 35:29

phrases.english: what is the reason it does not list them
in the order of their wisdom?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, וַיִּקְבְּרוּ אוֹתוֹ עֵשָׂו וְיַעֲקֹב בָּנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion from step 45.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that burial lists in the Torah follow the brothers' wisdom.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: At יצחק's burial, the less wise עשו is listed first, so wisdom is not what decides the order.

steps.title: ישמעאל let יצחק lead, so he did תשובה
steps.stepSummary: Since ישמעאל let יצחק go first, he treated him as leader, which proves he did תשובה in אברהם's lifetime.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since he let him go first, he made him his leader. And since he made him his leader, learn from this that he did תשובה in his father's days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the proof to its end. The order in the פסוק means ישמעאל let יצחק lead, and that shows he did תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order was not by wisdom, so it must show respect. ישמעאל was older, yet he let the younger יצחק go first. Giving his brother that honor shows a changed person, so he did תשובה while אברהם was still alive.
steps.whatToRemember: ישמעאל was older but let יצחק go first at אברהם's burial. That shows he did תשובה, so the rule of 'גויעה and אסיפה' for a צדיק still stands.

phrases.english: Rather, since he put him first,
he made him his leader,
and since he made him his leader,
learn from it that he repented in his days.
phrases.notes: "His days" means while his father אברהם was still alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the wisdom reading rejected, the גמרא confirms רבי יוחנן's proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ישמעאל did תשובה in אברהם's lifetime, so his death with 'גויעה' and 'אסיפה' fits the rule that this wording is used for a צדיק.

steps.title: A ברייתא begins: three who tasted the World to Come in this world
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא opens: הקב״ה gave three people a taste of עולם הבא already in this world.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Three people were given a taste by הקב״ה in this world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא. This line only sets it up, and the list of the three people comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties back to the earlier talk about אברהם being blessed 'with everything'. The ברייתא will name three people who got a taste of the reward of עולם הבא while still alive. The names and the source for each come in the next part.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
three people, the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave a taste
phrases.notes: A taste of what? The next line says: a taste of עולם הבא.

phrases.english: in this world

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה הִטְעִימָן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא linked to the earlier discussion of אברהם's blessing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three people were given a taste of עולם הבא in this world (the list comes next).
